title: Payment API pool exhaustion (pool 100→200)
symptoms: Checkout failing for users, returning 500 errors. Spikes in 5xx rate.
logs: Exception: ConnectionPoolExhausted: could not obtain a database connection within 5.000 seconds
recent_change: Increased marketing traffic due to promo email.
root_cause: Database connection pool limit (100) was reached during the traffic spike, preventing new requests from executing DB queries.
investigation: Checked application logs which showed ConnectionPoolExhausted. Monitored active DB connections and saw they were maxed at 100.
resolution: Increased application database connection pool size from 100 to 200 and restarted the service.
outcome: Error rate dropped to 0% and latency returned to normal (p99 < 200ms).
lesson: Ensure database connection pools are sized adequately for peak expected traffic. Implement connection wait timeouts safely.

title: Postgres replication lag 30s
symptoms: Users seeing stale data in analytics dashboards. Reports taking longer to generate.
metrics: Replica lag spiked from <1s to 30s. CPU on replica at 98%.
logs: WARNING: standby is taking too long to reply
recent_change: New indexing job was deployed that runs heavy analytical queries on the replica.
root_cause: The new analytical queries consumed all CPU on the read replica, causing it to fall behind on applying WAL logs from the primary.
investigation: Viewed Postgres replication stats and system CPU metrics. Identified the long-running queries locking resources.
resolution: Restarted the replica to drop connections, temporarily paused the indexing job, and later increased resources (CPU/RAM) for the read replica.
outcome: Replication lag caught up immediately after dropping connections.
lesson: Isolate heavy analytical workloads from standard read replicas, or ensure read replicas have sufficient resources to handle background jobs.

title: Memory leak in user service
symptoms: Service repeatedly crashing and restarting. Users intermittently unable to login.
metrics: JVM Heap usage climbing linearly over 4 hours until OOM crash.
recent_change: Deployed v2.4.1 which added a new local caching layer for user avatars.
root_cause: The new caching layer was not implementing an eviction policy, causing it to grow unboundedly until the JVM ran out of memory.
investigation: Took a heap dump before crash. Analyzed dump and found 80% of heap consumed by AvatarCache objects.
resolution: Applied a hotfix to add an LRU eviction policy to the cache and increased the JVM heap size slightly as a buffer.
outcome: Service stabilized with flat memory usage pattern around 40%.
lesson: Always implement strict limits and eviction policies for in-memory caches.

title: CPU spike on order service
symptoms: Orders not processing, queues backing up. High latency on order creation API.
metrics: CPU utilization on all Order Processing pods hit 100%.
logs: No explicit errors, but healthcheck endpoints timing out.
recent_change: Merged PR for new discount calculation logic.
root_cause: A logic bug in the discount calculator caused an infinite loop when applying multiple overlapping promotional codes.
investigation: Used profiling tools to identify the thread consuming the CPU. Traced it back to `calculate_compound_discount` function.
resolution: Deployed a hotfix to correct the loop termination condition and manually scaled up pods to clear the queue backlog.
outcome: CPU dropped to 15%, backlog cleared in 10 minutes.
lesson: Add timeout bounds to complex calculation loops and improve test coverage for edge cases like overlapping discounts.

title: API gateway timeout
symptoms: Mobile app users reporting 'Network Error' on launch.
metrics: Gateway 504 Gateway Timeout rate at 12%. Upstream response time > 5s.
logs: upstream timed out (110: Connection timed out) while reading response header from upstream
recent_change: None on Gateway. The upstream Product Service had a recent deployment.
root_cause: The Product Service became slow due to a missing DB index, causing it to exceed the Gateway's hardcoded 5-second timeout.
investigation: Traced 504s from Gateway to Product Service. Observed Product Service taking 6-7 seconds to respond.
resolution: Temporarily increased Gateway timeout to 10s. Simultaneously deployed the missing index to the Product Service.
outcome: Timeouts resolved, Product service latency improved to <100ms.
lesson: Gateway timeouts should be configurable without code deployment, and DB migrations should be reviewed for index requirements.

title: Deployment regression
symptoms: White screen of death for users on the checkout page.
metrics: JavaScript error rate spiked from 0% to 100% on /checkout path.
logs: TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'price')
root_cause: A missing null check on the new UI component caused the entire React tree to crash when loading items without a standard price field.
investigation: Checked Sentry logs for frontend errors. Matched the error to the exact PR merged 10 minutes prior.
resolution: Rolled back the deployment to the previous stable version.
outcome: Checkout page restored for all users within 5 minutes of rollback.
lesson: Implement better React Error Boundaries to prevent entire page crashes for isolated component failures.

title: Auth service failure
symptoms: No users can log in or obtain new session tokens.
metrics: Auth service success rate dropped to 0%.
root_cause: The internal SSL certificate used by the Auth service to communicate with the identity provider expired.
investigation: Checked Auth service logs. Verified certificate validity dates using OpenSSL.
resolution: Generated a new certificate, updated the secret in the orchestrator, and restarted the Auth pods.
outcome: Logins resumed successfully immediately after restart.
lesson: Implement automated certificate renewal and active monitoring for certificate expiration (e.g. 30 days before).

title: Redis cache failure
symptoms: High latency across multiple services. Cache miss rate 100%.
metrics: Redis memory usage 100%. Redis error rate 100%.
logs: OOM command not allowed when used memory > 'maxmemory'
recent_change: Enabled caching for new user feed feature.
root_cause: The Redis instance ran out of memory and the eviction policy was set to 'noeviction', preventing new writes.
investigation: Checked Redis metrics and saw memory flatlined at max. Attempted a manual write which failed with the OOM error.
resolution: Changed the eviction policy to 'allkeys-lru' and provisioned a larger Redis instance to handle the increased load.
outcome: Redis started evicting old keys, writes succeeded, and latency dropped.
lesson: Always configure a suitable eviction policy for caches and monitor memory usage trends when launching new features.

title: Network latency spike
symptoms: Intermittent timeouts between microservices in US-East region.
metrics: Inter-service p99 latency spiked from 5ms to 1200ms.
recent_change: Network team applied patches to Top-of-Rack switches.
root_cause: A bug in the new switch firmware caused packet drops under high load.
investigation: Isolated the issue to specific racks. Ran ping/mtr tests and saw 15% packet loss on the affected switches.
resolution: Rolled back the firmware update on the affected switches.
outcome: Packet loss ceased and latency returned to normal 5ms baseline.
lesson: Stagger infrastructure firmware updates to smaller blast radii (e.g. one rack at a time).

title: Disk full on logging service
symptoms: Logs not appearing in central dashboard.
logs: java.io.IOException: No space left on device
recent_change: Increased debug logging for a previous incident.
root_cause: The log rotation script failed because the disk filled up faster than the daily rotation schedule due to excessive debug logs.
investigation: SSH'd into the log aggregator node, ran `df -h` and saw /var/log at 100%.
resolution: Manually deleted old archives, fixed the log rotation config to run hourly, and disabled debug logging on the upstream service.
lesson: Set alerts for disk usage at 80% and configure rotation based on size, not just time.

title: Third-party payment gateway outage
symptoms: Users cannot complete purchases using credit cards.
metrics: Payment success rate dropped from 98% to 2%.
logs: ExternalAPIError: Stripe API responded with 503 Service Unavailable
root_cause: The primary payment provider experienced a widespread regional outage.
investigation: Checked the provider's status page which confirmed the outage. Our logs clearly showed 503s from their API.
resolution: Toggled the feature flag to failover to our secondary payment provider (PayPal/Braintree).
outcome: Purchases resumed using the backup provider.
lesson: Always maintain a hot standby for critical third-party dependencies and test the failover mechanism regularly.

title: Database deadlock
symptoms: Inventory updates failing, leading to overselling of items.
logs: ERROR: deadlock detected. Detail: Process 123 waits for ShareLock on transaction 456; blocked by process 789.
recent_change: New bulk inventory update feature released.
root_cause: Concurrent updates to the same rows in different orders caused transaction deadlocks in Postgres.
investigation: Analyzed Postgres lock traces. Found the bulk update script was sorting items inconsistently before applying updates.
resolution: Modified the application code to always sort item IDs before starting the update transaction.
outcome: Deadlocks ceased and inventory remained consistent.
lesson: Ensure all batch updates lock rows in a consistent, deterministic order to prevent deadlocks.

title: SSL certificate expiry
symptoms: All external clients failing to connect via HTTPS.
root_cause: The main domain SSL certificate expired because the automated Let's Encrypt cron job had failed silently a month ago.
investigation: Navigated to the API endpoint in a browser, verified certificate expiration date was today.
resolution: Manually ran Certbot to renew the certificate and restarted Nginx. Fixed the broken cron job.
lesson: Implement external synthetic monitoring that explicitly checks and alerts on certificate expiration dates.

title: Container OOM kills
symptoms: Large PDF reports failing to generate.
logs: dmesg shows: Memory cgroup out of memory: Killed process 1234 (node)
recent_change: Onboarded a new enterprise client with 10x the standard data volume.
root_cause: The Node.js process exceeded its Kubernetes pod memory limit (512Mi) when processing the massive new data set.
resolution: Increased the pod memory limit to 2Gi. Refactored the report generator to stream data instead of loading it all into memory.
outcome: Reports successfully generated for the large client without crashes.
lesson: Use streams for processing unbounded data sets to maintain predictable memory usage.

title: DNS resolution failures
symptoms: Services cannot communicate with each other via hostnames.
root_cause: The internal CoreDNS pods were overwhelmed by the sudden increase in query volume.
investigation: Checked CoreDNS metrics and saw high CPU and dropped packets.
resolution: Increased the number of CoreDNS replicas and implemented NodeLocal DNS cache.
outcome: DNS resolution latency dropped to <5ms, failures resolved.
lesson: Ensure core infrastructure components like DNS automatically scale alongside application workloads.

title: Message queue backlog
logs: Consumer pod logs show continuous CrashLoopBackOff
root_cause: The new library was incompatible with the older Node version in the container, causing consumers to crash on startup.
investigation: Checked consumer logs and found SyntaxError for unsupported JavaScript feature.
resolution: Reverted the library update, restarted consumers, and temporarily scaled consumers 5x to drain the backlog.
outcome: Queue drained in 30 minutes, normal delivery resumed.
lesson: Ensure CI/CD runs tests in the exact environment/container image used in production.

title: API rate limiting
symptoms: Legitimate users getting 429 Too Many Requests.
logs: RateLimitExceeded: client_ip hit limit of 1000 req/min
root_cause: The new partner was sending batch requests that easily exceeded our standard per-IP rate limit.
investigation: Analyzed access logs and identified the partner's IPs accounting for 90% of the 429s.
resolution: Added the partner's IP range to the rate limit whitelist and advised them to implement backoff.
outcome: Partner traffic succeeded, regular users unaffected.
lesson: Provision dedicated rate limits or API keys for known high-volume partners.

title: Database migration failure
symptoms: Deployments blocked, application throwing errors on new schema fields.
recent_change: Deploying v3.0 which renames a database column.
root_cause: The deployment ran the application code update before the database migration finished, causing the app to query a column that hadn't been renamed yet.
investigation: Reviewed the CI/CD pipeline logs and saw race condition between app deployment and migration job.
resolution: Rolled back the app code, ran the database migration manually, then redeployed the app code.
outcome: System stabilized, users can login again.
lesson: Never perform destructive DB changes (like renames) in a single step. Use the expand/contract pattern (add new column, write to both, switch reads, drop old).
